description: Single-panel line-and-marker plot of Vickers hardness versus annealing time for a cold-rolled Fe-22.5Mn-1.2Al-0.3C steel (Fig. 4, ref. [47]). The x-axis is labelled "Time, s" on a logarithmic scale with printed ticks at 0.1, 1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000 and 100000 s. The y-axis is labelled "Vickers hardness, HV" and runs from 150 to 450 HV with ticks every 50 HV. A grey legend box gives three entries: filled square "30%-630 °C", filled circle "40%-550 °C" and filled triangle "50%-550 °C". The 50%-550 °C curve is the hardest throughout, holding a near-plateau around the 430 HV level at short times before dropping steeply from about 1000 s down to roughly 190 HV at 100000 s. The 40%-550 °C curve starts near the 395-400 HV level, stays almost flat to about 10 s and falls to about 190 HV at the longest time. The 30%-630 °C curve starts lowest, near 335 HV, and declines monotonically, crossing roughly 300 HV around 100 s and ending near 145-150 HV at 100000 s. Several individual data points are ringed with ovals, and all three curves share a steep softening stage beginning between about 1000 and 3000 s. The figure demonstrates that higher cold-rolling reduction raises hardness while longer annealing progressively softens the steel.

subfigures.description: A single semi-log plot of Vickers hardness (HV, 150-450) against annealing time (0.1-100000 s) with three marker-coded curves: filled squares 30%-630 °C, filled circles 40%-550 °C and filled triangles 50%-550 °C. Hardness ranks 50% > 40% > 30% at short times; all curves soften steeply after roughly 1000-3000 s, converging near 150-190 HV at 100000 s. A few points are highlighted with oval rings.

observations.observation: The figure is a single plot with x-axis labelled 'Time, s' on a logarithmic scale (printed ticks 0.1, 1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000, 100000) and y-axis labelled 'Vickers hardness, HV' ranging 150 to 450 HV in ticks of 50 HV.
The legend contains exactly three entries: filled square '30%-630 °C', filled circle '40%-550 °C' and filled triangle '50%-550 °C'.

The 50%-550 °C curve (filled triangles) has the highest hardness of the three, holding a plateau near the 430 HV level at short times before falling steeply and ending at approximately 190 HV at 100000 s.
The 40%-550 °C curve (filled circles) starts near the 395-400 HV level, remains nearly flat to about 10 s, and then declines to roughly 190 HV at 100000 s.
The 30%-630 °C curve (filled squares) has the lowest hardness throughout, starting near 335 HV, passing about 300 HV around 100 s, and ending near 145-150 HV at 100000 s.
All three curves exhibit a steep softening stage that begins between roughly 1000 s and 3000 s.
Several individual data points on the curves are enclosed in oval rings, but the figure does not label what these highlighted points signify.
The caption states the figure shows the Vickers hardness evolution of 30%, 40% and 50% cold-rolled steels for different annealing times of Fe-22.5Mn-1.2Al-0.3C steel [47].
The citing text states that hardness was improved with increasing cold-rolling reduction due to high work hardening and decreased with increasing annealing time due to recrystallization.
The citing text attributes the study to Haase et al. [47] on a Fe-22.5Mn-1.2Al-0.3C steel with cold-rolling reductions of 30%, 40% and 50% and varying annealing time.
The hardness difference between the 30% and 50% cold-rolled conditions is largest at short annealing times and narrows considerably at the longest annealing time.
